title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 23
statement: A quadratic polynomial with real coefficients and leading coefficient \(1\) is called disrespectful if the equation \(p(p(x)) = 0\) is satisfied by exactly three real numbers. Among all the disrespectful quadratic polynomials, there is a unique such polynomial \(\tilde{p}(x)\) for which the sum of the roots is maximized. What is \(\tilde{p}(1)?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(p\) have roots \(r\) and \(s.\) Then \(p(p(x)) = 0\) splits into \(p(x) = r\) and \(p(x) = s,\) with discriminants \((r - s)^2 + 4r\) and \((r - s)^2 + 4s.\) Exactly three real roots means one discriminant is \(0\) and the other positive.

Take \((r - s)^2 + 4s = 0\) and set \(u = r - s.\) Then \(s = -\tfrac{u^2}{4}\) and the other discriminant is \(4u,\) so \(u>0.\) Also \(r+s=-\tfrac{u^2}{2}+u,\) maximized at \(u=1,\) giving \(r=\tfrac34\) and \(s=-\tfrac14.\)

So \(\tilde{p}(x) = \left(x - \tfrac34\right)\left(x + \tfrac14\right),\) and \(\tilde{p}(1) = \tfrac14\cdot\tfrac54 = \tfrac{5}{16}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: If \(p\) has roots \(r, s,\) then \(p(p(x)) = 0\) means \(p(x) = r\) or \(p(x) = s;\) exactly three roots requires one of these to have a double root
With \((r - s)^2 + 4s = 0\) and letting \(u = r - s,\) maximize \(r + s = -\tfrac{u^2}{2} + u\)
